> **Status: research / pre-alpha.** The design is specified in the PRD (v4) and the research paper; implementation is starting from zero, tracked as [`TR-01` … `TR-36`](https://github.com/orgs/trishula-dev/projects/1). Nothing here should be presumed working yet. This site documents what the project is building and why — it is research for adoption, not a product pitch.

## What Trishula is

Trishula is an open Web Application and API Firewall for Kubernetes that operates at **kernel altitude** while preserving the full userspace detection stack. Three components, two planes, one decision record per request:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph KERNEL["kernel plane"]
        xdp["eBPF shield<br/>XDP + TC"]
        maps["maps<br/>ACL · verdict cache · ban table"]
    end
    subgraph USER["userspace plane"]
        ing["ingest<br/>(ringbuf drain)"]
        lad["detection ladder<br/>S0-S6"]
    end
    gw["Gateway API<br/>(NGF reference)"] --> eng["engine"]
    eng --> app["app pods"]
    eng -- flows --> lad
    ing --> xdp
    xdp --- maps
    lad -- verdicts --> otel[("OTLP<br/>trishula.verdict.v1")]
```

- **kernel shield** — an XDP/TC eBPF program: L3/L4 ACLs, a verdict cache and a ban table with `TC_ACT_SHOT` drops, streaming flow events to userspace over a ring buffer. Bounded, tail-call-bounded parsing; verifier-checked in CI; fail-open by default.
- **userspace engine** — the detection ladder: S0 kernel pre-clear → S1 verdict cache → S2 CEL rules under cost budgets → S3 OWASP CRS via embedded Coraza → S4 OpenAPI positive security → S6 bot detection (JA4, header behaviour).
- **control plane** — `WAFPolicy` / `BanPolicy` CRDs compiled to engine bundles and shield maps; installed behind the Gateway API (NGF as the reference data plane); rollback as a CRD re-pin, never a hand-hack.

## Why

The WAF is the last security control that never crossed to developer ubiquity. Three curves converge:

1. **Gateway API consolidation** — ingress is standardising on the Gateway API; the edge is being re-plumbed.
2. **eBPF maturity** — kernel-altitude packet processing is now dependable, inspectable and CO-RE portable.
3. **AI traffic at the WAF's front door** — agents, scrapers and automated abuse hit exactly the layer the WAF inspects; they mint fingerprints machines can't hide behind.

Negative signatures alone cannot carry a modern estate. Trishula is built **developer-first**: CRD-driven policy, per-route promotion gates (learn → shadow → enforce), and honest, verifiable verdict telemetry — so the people who own the app can own its protection. The [research paper](docs/paper.qmd) states the full argument.

## Design principles

| Principle | Consequence |
|-----------|-------------|
| Two planes, one decision | Kernel drops what must be dropped; the engine runs the full detection stack; every verdict is recorded. |
| Parity, not a rewrite | CRS runs via embedded Coraza as the reference evaluator, with a CI-blocking differential suite. |
| Fail-open by default | The shield is inline but never a single point of failure; `failureMode` is explicit per policy. |
| Promotion gates | Any rule moves learn → shadow → enforce; shadow-first for every new detector. |
| Telemetry as a contract | Every verdict is a correlated OTel span + metric + log; dashboards ship in-repo. |
| Honest exit criteria | [Phase 0](docs/roadmap.qmd#phase-0-exit-criteria) pass/fail is stated, not implied. |
